note: Source of the ChatGPT plugin package (the ZIP OpenAI's dashboard takes). `pnpm chatgpt-plugin` builds it into .tmp/; `pnpm chatgpt-plugin --check` validates it. `tools` mirrors packages/mcp/src/annotations.ts and apps/api/src/chatgpt-plugin.test.ts keeps the two in step. The test cases run against the reviewer workspace that `pnpm db:seed-reviewer` fills (packages/core/src/reviewer-seed.ts). No credentials go in this file: the reviewer login is entered in the dashboard.

app_info.subtitle: Find leads, send cold email
app_info.description:
Meerko is an open-source outbound engine that ChatGPT runs for you. Tell ChatGPT who you sell to and it uses Meerko to find the right companies and people, find and verify their work emails, and write a short email sequence. Meerko sends it from your own Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook or any IMAP/SMTP mailbox, inside a send window and daily limits that keep your domain healthy, and stops writing to anyone who replies.

Replies come back to ChatGPT: Meerko handles bounces, unsubscribe requests and out-of-office replies on its own, and ChatGPT sorts the rest (interested, question, not now) and drafts an answer for each one. Each draft waits for your approval before it goes.

What you can ask:
- "Find 25 heads of growth at Series A fintechs in the US and get their emails."
- "Write a three-step sequence for them and show me the first email for each person."
- "Who replied this week? Draft answers to the interested ones."
- "How is my sequence doing?"

You need a Meerko account, which you create when you connect, and a mailbox connected in Meerko to send from. The code is AGPL-3.0, so you can also run the whole thing yourself.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates, edits, pauses, resumes and deletes the user's Autopilot routines (a saved brief plus when it runs); the list and get actions only read them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Routines are records in the user's own Meerko workspace. Run now starts the user's own AI through the trigger the user connected in the dashboard; the tool itself reaches nothing public.
justifications.destructive_justification: The delete action removes a routine for good, and update overwrites its name, brief and schedule.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records that a routine run has started, so it writes a run record, and returns the routine's brief.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes only to the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a run record and changes nothing that already exists.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns which workspace the connection acts on and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the workspaces the user belongs to and marks the current one, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves which of the user's workspaces this connection acts on from now on.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes a setting on the user's own Meerko connection and nothing outside it.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only moves a pointer between the user's workspaces; switching back restores it, and no data is removed or sent.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new, empty workspace for another brand.
justifications.open_world_justification: The workspace is private to the user's Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds a workspace; existing workspaces and their data are untouched, and the connection is not switched to the new one.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes a workspace's name.
justifications.open_world_justification: The name is only shown inside the user's own Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes a label only; no lead, sequence or email is removed or sent, and the name can be changed back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the workspace's lead tables with their columns and row counts, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new lead table in the workspace.
justifications.open_world_justification: The table is private to the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds a table; no existing table or row is changed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Adds a column to a table, or saves a new instruction for an existing AI column.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the table's definition in the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a column and leaves every row's values as they are; adding it again only replaces the column's instruction text.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the rows whose AI column is still empty, with the instruction for each, and writes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only rows in the user's own Meerko workspace. Meerko does not run the instruction or call any model.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Fetches a company's public home page and returns its title, description, headings and visible text. Nothing is saved or changed.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads any public website the user names, which is outside the user's Meerko account. Private and internal addresses are refused.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the workspace's saved ideal customer profile, or null when none is set.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves the workspace's ideal customer profile and rescores every lead against it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only a setting and the derived fit scores inside the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces a profile setting, which the user can set again at any time; leads, their data and their emails are kept, and the scores are recomputed from the profile.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves a manual adjustment of -30 to 30, with a note, on rows' ICP fit scores.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only scores inside the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: The adjustment sits on top of the rule-based score and clearing it restores that score; no lead data is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes values into existing rows of a table.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only rows in the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: A value written to a cell that already had one overwrites it, and the previous value is not kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Inserts new rows into a table, creating columns for keys it has not seen.
justifications.open_world_justification: The rows are stored in the user's own Meerko workspace and sent nowhere else.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds rows; existing rows are not changed or removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads rows from a table with their pipeline stage and ICP fit, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes leads (rows) from a table and stops their sequences.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletes only from the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: The rows are deleted permanently and cannot be restored.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a table with all its rows and its paused or draft sequences.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletes only from the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: The table, its rows and those sequences are deleted permanently and cannot be restored.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves the people it finds as new rows in a table and spends one credit per result. With count_only it only returns a number.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches a third-party database of business contacts, which is outside the user's Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds rows; nothing existing is changed or removed, and nobody is contacted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves the companies it finds as new rows in a table and spends one credit per result. With count_only it only returns a number.
justifications.open_world_justification: Searches a third-party database of companies, which is outside the user's Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds rows; nothing existing is changed or removed, and nobody is contacted.

justifications.read_only_justification: Writes the email, its certainty and verification result (or a phone number) into rows, and spends credits for each one found.
justifications.open_world_justification: Looks contact details up with third-party data providers, which are outside the user's Meerko account. No email is sent to the person.
justifications.destructive_justification: Fills rows that have no result yet. A row that already has one is only re-run when the caller passes overwrite, which the user asks for.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns whether credits are on and the current balance. It returns no plan, price or link to buy.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Starts connecting a mailbox to the workspace: it returns a sign-in link, or the steps for an app password, that the user completes in the browser. It is marked as a write because the flow it starts ends with a new mailbox in the workspace.
justifications.open_world_justification: It only hands the user a link to Meerko's connect page or to Google's or Microsoft's own sign-in; the tool itself contacts no mailbox and no password passes through the chat.
justifications.destructive_justification: Nothing is connected, removed or sent until the user finishes the sign-in themselves.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the connected sending mailboxes with their limits, ramp and status, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Changes a mailbox's daily send limit, sender name or ramp, or lifts a hold Meerko put on it.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only sending settings stored in the user's Meerko workspace; it sends no email itself.
justifications.destructive_justification: Changes settings that can be set back at any time; no mailbox, lead or email is removed.

justifications.read_only_justification: Looks up the SPF, DKIM and DMARC records of the domains the workspace sends from and reports what is missing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Queries public DNS, which is outside the user's Meerko account.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sends one test email from a connected mailbox to the address given.
justifications.open_world_justification: A real email leaves the user's mailbox for an inbox outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: A sent email cannot be taken back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new email sequence in draft status for a table.
justifications.open_world_justification: A draft is stored in the user's Meerko workspace and sends nothing.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds a draft sequence; no email goes out until leads are enrolled and the sequence is started with a separate tool.

justifications.read_only_justification: Edits a sequence's name, mailbox pool, send window or steps.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the sequence stored in the user's Meerko workspace; it sends no email itself.
justifications.destructive_justification: New steps replace all the existing ones and the previous text is not kept; removing a mailbox from the pool stops the leads that were mid-thread on it.

justifications.read_only_justification: Renders each step of a sequence for one row, as it would be sent, and saves nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace; nothing is sent.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Adds rows from the sequence's table to the sequence as enrollments.
justifications.open_world_justification: In a sequence that is already running, the enrolled people are emailed from the user's mailbox, at inboxes outside Meerko. In a draft or paused sequence nothing is sent until it is started.
justifications.destructive_justification: Enrolling into a running sequence leads to real emails, which cannot be taken back once sent. By default each email still waits for the user's approval.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets a sequence to active, so its emails start going out on schedule.
justifications.open_world_justification: Real emails go from the user's mailbox to the enrolled people's inboxes, outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: Emails that have been sent cannot be taken back; pausing only stops the ones not yet sent.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes a sequence with its steps and enrollments.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletes only from the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: The sequence, its steps and its enrollments are deleted permanently.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets a sequence to paused.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the sequence's status in the user's Meerko workspace; it stops email rather than sending it.
justifications.destructive_justification: Pausing keeps every step and enrollment and is undone by starting the sequence again.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns whether the user approves each email or Meerko sends on its own. The setting is only changed in the dashboard.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the sequence emails waiting for the user's approval, as each lead would get them.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace; nothing is sent.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Marks leads' next sequence email as approved, which releases it to be sent when due.
justifications.open_world_justification: The approved emails go from the user's mailbox to people's inboxes outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: Once an approved email has been sent it cannot be taken back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the workspace's sequences with their status and enrollment counts.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a sequence's enrollment states, emails sent, reply rate and mailbox pool usage.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only figures stored in the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists replies to the user's sequences with the thread and the lead's row, changing nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads replies Meerko has already stored in the user's workspace; the tool does not contact the mailbox provider.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves an intent on a reply (interested, question, not now and so on) and can mark it handled.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only a label in the user's Meerko workspace; the person who replied sees nothing.
justifications.destructive_justification: Sets a label that can be set again; the reply itself is kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Saves a draft answer to a reply for the user to review.
justifications.open_world_justification: In a workspace the user has switched to automatic sending, the draft is emailed at once to the person who replied, outside Meerko. By default it is only stored, and sending is the separate approve_draft tool.
justifications.destructive_justification: With automatic sending on, the draft goes out as a real email, which cannot be taken back. Drafting again for the same reply also replaces the pending draft's text.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the reply drafts waiting for the user, with the reply and thread each one answers.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sends a draft as a reply in the email thread, from the user's mailbox.
justifications.open_world_justification: A real email goes to the inbox of the person who replied, outside Meerko.
justifications.destructive_justification: A sent email cannot be taken back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a pending reply draft.
justifications.open_world_justification: Deletes only from the user's own Meerko workspace; nothing is sent.
justifications.destructive_justification: The draft's text is discarded and cannot be restored.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns lead counts per pipeline stage, for one table or the whole workspace.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the user's own Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Read-only: it deletes, overwrites and sends nothing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Sets the pipeline stage of the given leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only a field in the user's Meerko workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: A stage is a label that can be moved back; the lead and its history are kept.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates or updates contacts in the CRM the user connected (HubSpot or Attio) from the table's leads.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes to a third-party CRM, which is outside Meerko, with the access the user granted in the dashboard.
justifications.destructive_justification: Contacts are matched by email and created or updated with the lead's fields; it deletes no contact and sends no message.

test_cases.description: Read the lead tables and the leads in one of them.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which lead tables do I have in Meerko? Show me the people in the demo one.
test_cases.expected_output: Names the table "Demo leads: B2B SaaS founders" with 8 rows, then lists its eight leads with name, title and company (for example Maya Okafor, Founder & CEO at Ledgerline, and Jonas Berg, VP Sales at Fjordly) and each one's pipeline stage. Nothing is changed.

test_cases.description: Preview a sequence email as a lead would receive it, without sending anything.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me my Meerko sequences and how the first email reads for one of the leads.
test_cases.expected_output: Shows one sequence, "Founders: agent-run outbound", paused, with 6 leads enrolled. Then shows its three steps rendered for one lead: the first has a subject like "Ledgerline and outbound, Maya" and a body that opens with the lead's first name, and the two follow-ups come 3 and 4 days later. No email is sent.

test_cases.description: Find the reply nobody has sorted yet and classify it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Do I have new replies in Meerko? Mark the one from Maya as a question.
test_cases.expected_output: Shows one unsorted reply, from Maya Okafor at Ledgerline, asking whether Meerko works with Claude or only ChatGPT, then confirms it is now classified as a question. No email is sent.

test_cases.description: Review the reply drafts that are waiting for the user's approval.
test_cases.user_prompt: Show me the reply drafts waiting for my approval in Meerko.
test_cases.expected_output: Lists two pending drafts with the reply each one answers: one to Maya Okafor about working with Claude, and one to Tomás Rivera about pricing for a team of three and using their own Gmail inboxes. It says they have not been sent and asks before sending any.

test_cases.description: Write a draft answer to an interested reply and leave it for review.
test_cases.user_prompt: Priya replied that she is interested. Draft a short answer in Meerko proposing Thursday at 3pm, and don't send it yet.
test_cases.expected_output: Finds the reply from Priya Nair at Quaystack ("Yes, let's talk. Thursday afternoon works for me."), saves a short draft that proposes Thursday at 3pm, shows its text and says it is waiting for approval. Nothing is sent.

test_cases.description: Report the pipeline and how the sequence is doing.
test_cases.user_prompt: How is my outbound going in Meerko? Give me the pipeline and the numbers for my sequence.
test_cases.expected_output: Reports the pipeline for the demo workspace: 2 new, 3 contacted and 3 replied leads, none in meeting, won or lost. For the sequence "Founders: agent-run outbound" it reports 6 leads enrolled, 6 emails sent and 3 replies, and that the sequence is paused.

test_cases.description: Count matching leads in the lead database without saving them or spending credits.
test_cases.user_prompt: With Meerko, how many CTOs at fintech companies in Spain could I reach? Just count them, don't save anything.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the number of people matching a CTO title at financial-services companies in Spain. It says the count is free, and no rows are saved and no credits are spent.

test_cases.description: Show the credit balance, with no offer to buy more.
test_cases.user_prompt: How many Meerko credits do I have left?
test_cases.expected_output: States the workspace's credit balance as a number (about 2,000 in the demo workspace, less whatever earlier searches used). The answer has no prices, plans or links to buy credits.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for the user's general inbox. Meerko reads only replies to the sequences it sent, not the rest of a mailbox.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Summarise the unread emails that arrived in my inbox this morning.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Meerko should not be invoked. If asked about it, ChatGPT explains that Meerko only shows replies to its own sequences.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for social media. Meerko sends email and has no tool that posts or sends messages on social networks.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing our seed round and publish it on my profile.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Meerko should not be invoked, because it cannot post to LinkedIn or any social network.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for general knowledge about sales or email with nothing to look up or do in the user's workspace.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What is a good reply rate for B2B cold email, and what is the difference between SPF and DKIM?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: Meerko should not be invoked: this is a general question, answered from ChatGPT's own knowledge.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not sell anything. Meerko has no tool that buys credits or changes a plan, and returns no checkout link.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Buy me 5,000 more Meerko credits and upgrade my plan.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: No purchase is made and no checkout or upgrade link is shown. At most ChatGPT reads the current balance and says that credits and plans are managed in the user's Meerko account settings.

plugin.note: Fields only the plugin package needs; the rest of the package is derived from app_info and the test cases above. `name` is the package id of a first upload: once the dashboard has a listing, the id it assigned may have to go here instead, or the upload is refused. `developerName` is replaced by the verified identity on the dashboard. `demoRecordingURL` stays null until the walkthrough video exists; the package builds without it but cannot be submitted.
plugin.name: meerko
defaultPrompt: Find 25 heads of growth at Series A fintechs in the US and get their emails.
Who replied this week? Draft answers to the interested ones.
plugin.releaseNotes: First release: find companies and people, find and verify work emails, send sequences from your own mailbox, and sort and answer replies, with every email waiting for your approval by default.
